title: Great Pyramid of Cholula (Tlachihualtepetl)
summary: The Great Pyramid of Cholula, in central Mexico, is a vast stepped platform built over centuries in successive layers, the first from the 2nd century BC. Its final form covered more than 1,300 feet a side and stood almost 213 feet high, making it the largest temple base of the pre-Hispanic world. INAH says it was abandoned around the end of the 8th century; McCafferty describes only a partial abandonment in the Early Postclassic, with the pyramid remaining a shrine until the Spanish Conquest.

uncertainty.note: INAH says the first Great Pyramid dates to the second century BC (so -199 to -100); no date is given for the final enlargement. End is the present: the mound survives. Abandonment is placed at the end of the eighth century (about 799).

footprint.description: A square base enlarged over three main stages: about 427 feet a side in the first stage, about 558 feet in the second (nine stepped sections, almost 148 feet tall), and more than 1,300 feet a side in the final one. Register figures only.

phases.description: First Great Pyramid in the second century BC; enlarged over a second and then a final pyramid. INAH gives no dates for the later stages, only that it was in use until the end of the eighth century.
The sanctuary was destroyed, sacked and abandoned after wars and a Popocatepetl eruption (INAH, undated within the 8th-century crisis); adobe crumbled and the pyramid took on the look of a hill.

materials.material: compacted adobe blocks stuck with mud, with a stucco coat painted in bright colours

reviewer_note: Shape stepped_pyramid (the final stage's outline is a stepped hill-like pyramid). Base is 'more than 1,300 ft', a floor not an exact side; height is the stage average without the temple. Only INAH was opened as a heritage source; other sources give 300-450 m per side, so base and height are the least certain. Thin sourcing: one government page plus OSM for coordinates.
